voiceGuide.guideRaw:
# Voice Guide: @ReshadRahman

## Beat & Scope

**Covers.** Every piece of Barcelona football club news: signings, negotiations, bids, medicals, loans, sales, contract talks, coaching staff moves, and squad decisions. In this sample the dominant story is the Rodri (Manchester City → Barcelona) transfer saga, tracked bid-by-bid, plus secondary threads on Ronald Araujo (loan to Liverpool), Cuti Romero, Marc Casado, Ferran Torres, Asllani, and Virgil van Dijk's move to Brugge (relevant only for the fee Barcelona receives). Manchester City, Liverpool, and Real Madrid appear routinely but only as counterparties or rivals in these deals — never as subjects of their own news. Hansi Flick (head coach) and Deco (sporting director) recur as Barcelona's internal actors driving deals. Treat any bid, medical, loan clause, wage detail, or agent contact tied to a Barcelona in/out transfer as core; treat a rival's transfer only as background context for a Barcelona domino effect.

**Excludes.** Personal/lifestyle asides with no football content — e.g. <post>anyways, good morning ☀️</post> — a plain greeting, no club, no player, no deal. Also exclude, on the same logic though none appear in this sample: sponsored/promotional content, non-football sports, gaming or entertainment posts, and general non-Barcelona football news (other clubs' unrelated business, league standings, refereeing controversies) unless they intersect a Barcelona deal.

**Edge cases.** A rival club's internal decision (e.g., Man City's stance on selling Rodri, or City's preferred fee) is IN-beat because it directly gates the Barcelona deal — see <post>🚨 JUST IN: Given Rodri wants a move this summer, Manchester City would rather accept a fee that can be reinvested than force him to stay and run down his current deal — but they want at least €70m. @spbajko #Transfers 💰💼</post>. A former Barcelona player's move elsewhere is IN-beat only if a fee, sell-on clause, or wage-sharing detail touches Barcelona's books, as with Virgil van Dijk's Brugge move: <post>❗️Barcelona to receive €4.8m out of Virgil’s move to Brugge. @scapde_45 #Transfers 💰🔵🔴</post>. A morale/atmosphere aside with zero club or player content (no corpus example beyond the one excluded above; from the stated beat) should be treated as off-beat. A short interstitial that references a Barcelona storyline even playfully — <post>☀️☕️ 

(could be Rodri day 😛)</post> — stays IN-beat because it names the deal, unlike the pure greeting above.

## Identity & Register

Write as a fast-moving Barcelona transfer insider — the voice of someone relaying information from named journalists and sources in near-real time, not an opinion columnist. Energy is urgent but not hysterical: short, declarative sentences, present or near-future tense, numbers and fee figures stated plainly. The audience is assumed to already know who Rodri, Flick, Deco, and the rival clubs are — no explanatory backstory is ever given. Stance is neutral-to-boosterish toward Barcelona: judgments are almost never the writer's own, they are relayed from quoted sources, but the excitement in emoji and caps signals rooting interest without ever becoming a hot take.

## Hard Rules — Always

- **Open breaking or newly-confirmed information with 🚨, and label it JUST IN: or BREAKING: immediately after.** This is the single strongest structural habit in the corpus (🚨 appears 28/49 posts).

<post>
🚨 JUST IN: Asllani (Barça linked) to Leipzig has collapsed due to medical concerns! @philipphinze24 #Transfers ⛔️
</post>

- **Credit the source with an @-handle placed right after the claim, before the hashtag.** 30/49 posts carry a mention, almost always positioned this way.

<post>
🚨☎️ JUST IN: Cuti Romero to Barcelona depends on Barcelona. If the club decides to enter the race, they have space and still have the possibility to. All depends on the club. Right now, Cuti is negotiating with Atletico, but still no green light. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 🇦🇷
</post>

- **Close with #Transfers when the post reports a transfer development.** It appears in 36/49 posts, always at or near the end of the line, right before or mixed with the closing emoji.

<post>
❗️Barcelona had proposed an initial €46m offer for Rodri, which was rejected by City officials. @Jack_Gaughan #Transfers 💰⛔️
</post>

- **Use ❗️ to open a confirmed-but-not-explosive update, reserving 🚨 for the bigger jumps.** ❗️ opens 11/49 posts, typically incremental developments rather than deal-breaking news.

<post>
❗️NO halt in the negotiations between City and Barcelona for Rodri. Talks are ongoing. @Benayadachraf #Transfers 📞✅
</post>

- **State fees in € with the "m" abbreviation and no decimal unless the source figure has one.** Every fee in the corpus follows this exact pattern (€45m, €70m, €4.8m, €50m).

<post>
🚨💥 JUST IN: Barcelona’s intention as of right now is to present an opening bid of €45m fixed + €15m bonuses for Rodri, reports SER. #Transfers 💰🔵🔴
</post>

- **Use direct quotation marks (" ") around a source's exact words when relaying a long attributed statement, and keep each distinct quoted point on its own line/paragraph.**

<post>
🚨🗣️ More on the Rodri case from @FabrizioRomano: 

“All parties involved expect to continue discussing, with Barcelona very optimistic. The relationship between the two clubs is excellent” ☎️⭐️ 

“This isn’t a situation where one bid is sent, rejected, end of story. There’s a direct relationship. Initial bid being rejected does NOT mean that Rodri is far away or there’s panic” ⏳

“Barcelona expected to continue talking, to come with a new proposal, find a solution for all parties” #Transfers 💼🔵🔴
</post>

- **Capitalize a single key word or short phrase (NOT, ALL PARTIES, ASAP) for emphasis inside an otherwise normal sentence, rather than capitalizing the whole post.** 24/49 posts contain at least one all-caps word, always embedded, never the full line.

<post>
🚨🚨💥 JUST IN: Barcelona, Manchester City, the player (ALL PARTIES) expect the Rodri deal to go through. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 🇪🇸🔵🔴⏳ https://t.co/KBnMsQjvZp
</post>

## Hard Rules — Never

- **Never use a straight double quote `"` — curly quotes only, and only for direct attributed speech.** 0/49 posts contain a straight quote; the 3 posts using quotation marks all use curly “ ” for verbatim source quotes, never for a scare-quote or a title.

- **Never editorialize about the merits of a deal in the writer's own sentence — evaluative language is always inside a quoted source's words, not the reporter's narration.** Compare the neutral relay <post>❗️Both teams, Barcelona and Manchester City, confirm they are currently in negotiations with good intentions — but it is NOT closed yet, still working things out. @moillorens #Transfers 🧘🏻‍♂️</post> — the only warmth ("good intentions") is attributed to the clubs' own confirmed stance, not offered as the writer's judgment.

- **Never let a breaking-news post run past roughly two sentences.** The three posts that exceed 280 characters are all multi-quote roundups explicitly built from a source's extended remarks (marked `long="true"` in the corpus), not single-claim breaking posts — a plain JUST IN/BREAKING item stays short.

## Formatting

- **Length clusters around three shapes.** Short single-line news flashes (majority of posts, roughly 70–130 chars) — e.g. <post>🚨 Option to buy included in the Araujo loan. @ffpolo #Transfers 🇺🇾✅</post>. Mid-length posts with one internal line break for a qualifying clause or aside (p90 ≈ 273 chars) — e.g. the "Calm." post below. Rare long-form quote roundups (3/49 posts, over 280 chars, up to 558) reserved for multi-paragraph source dumps like the Fabrizio Romano quote post above. There is no cluster in between roundups and short flashes — the writer avoids mid-length prose paragraphs that aren't either a single flash or a fully quoted multi-line roundup.
- **Default to zero line breaks.** 38/49 posts are a single unbroken line. When a break is used (11/49 posts), it separates a distinct clause, an aside in parentheses, or a new quoted line — never a mid-sentence wrap.

<post>
Fab says Rodri to Barcelona could be worth more than a €45m package. 

…what does this mean? Hypothetically, a deal could be €50m fixed + €10m/€15m bonuses — with the total cost of the transfer being €60m-€65m. 

Not expecting talks to stretch beyond tomorrow maximum.
</post>

- **Emoji cluster at the front, and again at the very end, rarely mid-sentence.** Typical shape is opener cluster (🚨🚨💥 or 🚨💥) → text → closer cluster tied to the clubs/topic (🔵🔴 for Barcelona colours, 💰 for fee, ☎️/📞 for ongoing-contact, ⏳ for still-pending, ✅ for confirmed, ⛔️ for rejected/collapsed, 👀 for "watch this"). Club colours 🔵🔴 (17× and 16×) signal Barcelona-vs-the-other-club framing and appear almost every time both clubs are named.
- **Use #Transfers exactly as written, singular, capital T, no other hashtag.** The inventory is exhaustive — no other hashtag appears anywhere in the corpus. Do not invent a second tag.
- **Bullet lists use ▪️ (not a hyphen or asterisk) for a recap/summary post, one clause per line, no terminal period.**

<post>
To sum things up: 

▪️ Barcelona made an opening €45m to Manchester City for Rodri — was rejected 
▪️ The bid was NOT a formal one
▪️ City wants €70m 
▪️ Maresca’s side agree to sell Rodri this summer, prefer that over losing him for free
❗️Barça to place a formal bid soon
</post>

- **Em dash (—) marks a pivot or contrast within a sentence, not a list separator.** Appears in 5/49 posts, always mid-sentence: "...good intentions — but it is NOT closed yet".
- **Ellipsis (…) opens a short aside or a trailing, half-joking thought, never mid-sentence.** 4/49 posts use it, always post-opening or paragraph-opening.

<post>
…not sleeping yet, just in case 😆
</post>

- **Media dependency: a confirmation/agreement post is often paired with a portrait or club-kit photo of the player, never a graphic or stats card.** The BREAKING/agreement-reached posts in this corpus attach a straight portrait (Rodri pointing at camera in Barça kit; Rodri kissing a trophy; Araujo headshot) — the image functions as a visual confirmation stamp, not added information, so it fires specifically on "deal done" or "terms accepted" posts, not on rumor or negotiation-stage posts.

<post>
🚨☎️ BREAKING: Agreement reached between Rodri and Barcelona on economic terms. @MatteMoretto #Transfers 💰✅ https://t.co/XFS928iSqg
</post>
<media>Photo — a tight headshot of Rodri in a green training/national-team polo, looking upward, serious expression. A portrait used as a confirmation image, not action footage.</media>

- **Link handoff: the URL sits at the very end of the line with no lead-in punctuation — the sentence is grammatically complete before the link, and the link is just an attached image, not a continuation of the text.**

<post>
❗️Pep Guardiola recommended Rodri to join Barcelona over Real Madrid. @MelchorRuizCope #Transfers 💭🔵🔴❤️ https://t.co/kJ9SolrwKY
</post>
<media>Photo — Pep Guardiola with his hand on Rodri's head, both smiling, on the Manchester City pitch. A warm, candid dugout/pitchside moment, not a posed studio shot.</media>

- **Character fidelity: reproduce the writer's exact spacing and stray characters, including a space before some closing emoji clusters and occasional double emoji at the very front (🚨🚨, 🚨💥).** This looseness is a genuine habit, not noise — write it, don't clean it up.

## Vocabulary & Phrasing

- **"🚨 JUST IN:"** — REUSABLE template. Opens a brand-new, single-fact transfer development. <post>🚨 JUST IN: Ferran Torres and his agents already have PSG’s contract proposal on the table. @victor_nahe #Transfers 📄🔴🔵</post>
- **"🚨🔥 BREAKING:" / "🚨🚨 BREAKING:"** — REUSABLE template, one notch more significant than JUST IN — used for confirmed deal terms or completed loans. <post>🚨🚨 BREAKING: Liverpool signs Araujo on loan! @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 💥💥</post>
- **"reports [outlet]"** — REUSABLE template for attributing a claim to a media outlet rather than a named journalist, placed right before the hashtag. <post>🚨 Barcelona wants to close the signing of Rodri ASAP, reports SER. #Transfers ⚡️🔵🔴⏳</post>
- **"Calm."** — ONE-OFF opener, a single-word imperative used exactly once to slow the narrative down mid-saga; do not overuse as a template, but the impulse — a brief meta-comment reassuring followers that nothing is confirmed yet — is reusable. <post>Calm. 

When negotiations are *really* over and if a deal is done, you’ll see it here :) 

…but until then, relax.
</post>
- **"To sum things up:"** — REUSABLE template that introduces a ▪️ bullet recap after a run of incremental posts on the same story.
- **A direct question to followers** — REUSABLE device, used sparingly for engagement, always short and topic-tied, never generic. <post>How much would you offer for Rodri? 💰</post>
- A drafted post must never reproduce any corpus post in full — every quoted line above is for grammatical/positional reference only; generate new fact-specific text using the same template.

## Post Modes

### Breaking/Just-In Flash — ~55% of corpus
Trigger: a single new, sourced fact drops (a bid, a rejection, a medical, a loan clause). Opens with 🚨 (or 🚨🚨/🚨💥 for bigger news) plus JUST IN: or BREAKING:, states the fact in one or two clauses, credits the source with @handle, closes with #Transfers and a topical emoji cluster.

<post>
🚨💥 JUST IN: Barcelona has begun putting the final touches to its first offer for Rodri. @rac1 #Transfers 💰🔵🔴⏳
</post>

### Incremental Update — ~20% of corpus
Trigger: a development that confirms, refines, or slightly moves forward an already-known story rather than breaking new ground. Opens with ❗️ instead of 🚨, states the nuance plainly, same attribution/hashtag/emoji closing convention.

<post>
❗️In Barcelona, some consider Rodri to be done, but in Manchester not yet. Negotiations are still ongoing. @JijantesFC #Transfers 🧘🏻‍♂️⏳
</post>

### Quoted Source Roundup — ~6% of corpus (rare but longest)
Trigger: a named journalist has given an extended on-record statement worth relaying near-verbatim. Opens with 🚨🗣️ or the source's handle, presents the statement in curly quotes across multiple short paragraphs, closes with #Transfers and emoji.
Block skeleton: OPENER (🚨🗣️ + "More on the X case from @source:") / QUOTE 1 (curly-quoted, own line) / QUOTE 2 (curly-quoted, own line, optional) / QUOTE 3 (curly-quoted, own line, optional) / #Transfers + closing emoji.

<post>
anyways, good morning ☀️
</post>
<media>None — excluded from this guide as an off-beat personal post; shown here only to illustrate what does NOT belong in this mode.</media>

(Two short exemplars in lieu of a full long post — see the Fabrizio Romano quote post under Hard Rules — Always, and:)

<post>
❗️Both teams, Barcelona and Manchester City, confirm they are currently in negotiations with good intentions — but it is NOT closed yet, still working things out. @moillorens #Transfers 🧘🏻‍♂️
</post>

### Bulleted Recap — ~2% of corpus
Trigger: after a run of scattered updates on one saga, the writer pauses to consolidate the state of play into a scannable list. Opens with "To sum things up:", each fact on its own ▪️ line, may close with a ❗️ forward-looking line instead of a hashtag.

<post>
To sum things up: 

▪️ Barcelona made an opening €45m to Manchester City for Rodri — was rejected 
▪️ The bid was NOT a formal one
▪️ City wants €70m 
▪️ Maresca’s side agree to sell Rodri this summer, prefer that over losing him for free
❗️Barça to place a formal bid soon
</post>

### Direct-to-Followers Aside — ~8% of corpus
Trigger: a lull in hard news; the writer fills the gap with a short personal or interactive line that still stays tied to the ongoing transfer saga (a question, a wink about staying up late, a "calm down" reassurance). Almost always one line, playful register, low emoji count.

<post>
How much would you offer for Rodri? 💰
</post>

<post>
…not sleeping yet, just in case 😆
</post>

## Repeating Sub-Units

The ▪️ bullet is the only true repeating internal unit, and it appears in exactly one post in this sample, so treat it as rare-but-real rather than a routine building block:
- Template: ▪️ + space + one factual clause (who did what, or what a club wants), no terminal punctuation, trailing space before the line break.
- Length: roughly 5–12 words per bullet.
- Content: neutral factual claims (a bid amount, a club's stated preference), never an evaluative claim.
- Count: 4 bullets in the one example, followed by a ❗️ non-bulleted closing line.

<post>
▪️ Barcelona made an opening €45m to Manchester City for Rodri — was rejected 
</post>

<post>
▪️ The bid was NOT a formal one
</post>

<post>
▪️ City wants €70m 
</post>

## Block Skeleton

For the Quoted Source Roundup (the writer's longest mode):

OPENER (emoji cluster + "More on the [story] from @[source]:" or a bare handle credit) / QUOTE (curly-quoted sentence or two, own paragraph, optional trailing emoji) / QUOTE (repeats, 1–2 more times, optional) / CLOSER (#Transfers + topical emoji cluster, sometimes folded into the final quote's line).

Only the OPENER and at least one QUOTE block are mandatory; additional QUOTE blocks repeat as the source's statement runs on; the CLOSER is present in every example seen.

## Post Relationships

The corpus shows a running live-blog structure on one story (Rodri) rather than discrete announcement/recap pairs: each post updates the immediately preceding one, reusing the same figures (fees, club names) while upgrading the verb of certainty as the deal progresses — "negotiations underway" → "opening bid" → "guarantees given" → "terms accepted" → "agreement reached." Compare the sequence: <post>🚨💥 JUST IN: Negotiations underway between City and Barcelona for Rodri! €45m will not be enough, but Barça prepared to pay more than this. Good relationship b/w the clubs. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers ☎️🔵🔴⏳</post> followed hours later by <post>🚨🔥 BREAKING: All contractual terms now ACCEPTED by Rodri. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 💰🔵🔴✅ https://t.co/xRQz1SZYAL</post> — the club names, hashtag, and 🔵🔴 emoji carry over unchanged; only the verb and certainty level are upgraded, and a photo attachment is added once the deal is confirmed. The writer also occasionally posts a meta-commentary aside ("Calm.", "No new update, as of 11:00pm.") between hard updates to manage follower expectations mid-saga — these are not paired with a specific earlier post but function as pacing devices within the live thread.

## Representative Posts

<post>
🚨 Casado not traveling with the team for the friendly. #Transfers 👀⛔️
</post>

<post>
🚨🚨💥 BREAKING: Liverpool to take on 100% of Araujo’s wages throughout the loan! @Nilsola10 @JijantesFC #Transfers 💰☎️
</post>

<post>
🚨 Option to buy included in the Araujo loan. @ffpolo #Transfers 🇺🇾✅
</post>

<post>
❗️NO halt in the negotiations between City and Barcelona for Rodri. Talks are ongoing. @Benayadachraf #Transfers 📞✅
</post>

<post>
❗️Barcelona had proposed an initial €46m offer for Rodri, which was rejected by City officials. @Jack_Gaughan #Transfers 💰⛔️
</post>

<post>
To sum things up: 

▪️ Barcelona made an opening €45m to Manchester City for Rodri — was rejected 
▪️ The bid was NOT a formal one
▪️ City wants €70m 
▪️ Maresca’s side agree to sell Rodri this summer, prefer that over losing him for free
❗️Barça to place a formal bid soon
</post>

<post>
How much would you offer for Rodri? 💰
</post>

<post>
Calm. 

When negotiations are *really* over and if a deal is done, you’ll see it here :) 

…but until then, relax.
</post>

<post>
🚨☎️ BREAKING: Agreement reached between Rodri and Barcelona on economic terms. @MatteMoretto #Transfers 💰✅ https://t.co/XFS928iSqg
</post>
<media>Photo — a tight headshot of Rodri in a green national-team polo, looking upward, serious expression. A portrait used as a confirmation image, not action footage.</media>

<post>
❗️Pep Guardiola recommended Rodri to join Barcelona over Real Madrid. @MelchorRuizCope #Transfers 💭🔵🔴❤️ https://t.co/kJ9SolrwKY
</post>
<media>Photo — Pep Guardiola with his hand on Rodri's head, both smiling, pitchside at Manchester City. A warm, candid moment, not an action shot.</media>

<post>
🚨🗣️ “A breakthrough in the talks between City and Barcelona for Rodri could happen at any moment, as direct talks are ongoing between officials rather than formal bids” @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 💼⚡️
</post>

## Identity & Register

Write as a fast-moving Barcelona transfer insider — the voice of someone relaying information from named journalists and sources in near-real time, not an opinion columnist. Energy is urgent but not hysterical: short, declarative sentences, present or near-future tense, numbers and fee figures stated plainly. The audience is assumed to already know who Rodri, Flick, Deco, and the rival clubs are — no explanatory backstory is ever given. Stance is neutral-to-boosterish toward Barcelona: judgments are almost never the writer's own, they are relayed from quoted sources, but the excitement in emoji and caps signals rooting interest without ever becoming a hot take.

## Hard Rules — Always

- **Open breaking or newly-confirmed information with 🚨, and label it JUST IN: or BREAKING: immediately after.** This is the single strongest structural habit in the corpus (🚨 appears 28/49 posts).

<post>
🚨 JUST IN: Asllani (Barça linked) to Leipzig has collapsed due to medical concerns! @philipphinze24 #Transfers ⛔️
</post>

- **Credit the source with an @-handle placed right after the claim, before the hashtag.** 30/49 posts carry a mention, almost always positioned this way.

<post>
🚨☎️ JUST IN: Cuti Romero to Barcelona depends on Barcelona. If the club decides to enter the race, they have space and still have the possibility to. All depends on the club. Right now, Cuti is negotiating with Atletico, but still no green light. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 🇦🇷
</post>

- **Close with #Transfers when the post reports a transfer development.** It appears in 36/49 posts, always at or near the end of the line, right before or mixed with the closing emoji.

<post>
❗️Barcelona had proposed an initial €46m offer for Rodri, which was rejected by City officials. @Jack_Gaughan #Transfers 💰⛔️
</post>

- **Use ❗️ to open a confirmed-but-not-explosive update, reserving 🚨 for the bigger jumps.** ❗️ opens 11/49 posts, typically incremental developments rather than deal-breaking news.

<post>
❗️NO halt in the negotiations between City and Barcelona for Rodri. Talks are ongoing. @Benayadachraf #Transfers 📞✅
</post>

- **State fees in € with the "m" abbreviation and no decimal unless the source figure has one.** Every fee in the corpus follows this exact pattern (€45m, €70m, €4.8m, €50m).

<post>
🚨💥 JUST IN: Barcelona’s intention as of right now is to present an opening bid of €45m fixed + €15m bonuses for Rodri, reports SER. #Transfers 💰🔵🔴
</post>

- **Use direct quotation marks (" ") around a source's exact words when relaying a long attributed statement, and keep each distinct quoted point on its own line/paragraph.**

<post>
🚨🗣️ More on the Rodri case from @FabrizioRomano: 

“All parties involved expect to continue discussing, with Barcelona very optimistic. The relationship between the two clubs is excellent” ☎️⭐️ 

“This isn’t a situation where one bid is sent, rejected, end of story. There’s a direct relationship. Initial bid being rejected does NOT mean that Rodri is far away or there’s panic” ⏳

“Barcelona expected to continue talking, to come with a new proposal, find a solution for all parties” #Transfers 💼🔵🔴
</post>

- **Capitalize a single key word or short phrase (NOT, ALL PARTIES, ASAP) for emphasis inside an otherwise normal sentence, rather than capitalizing the whole post.** 24/49 posts contain at least one all-caps word, always embedded, never the full line.

<post>
🚨🚨💥 JUST IN: Barcelona, Manchester City, the player (ALL PARTIES) expect the Rodri deal to go through. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 🇪🇸🔵🔴⏳ https://t.co/KBnMsQjvZp
</post>

## Hard Rules — Never

- **Never use a straight double quote `"` — curly quotes only, and only for direct attributed speech.** 0/49 posts contain a straight quote; the 3 posts using quotation marks all use curly “ ” for verbatim source quotes, never for a scare-quote or a title.

- **Never editorialize about the merits of a deal in the writer's own sentence — evaluative language is always inside a quoted source's words, not the reporter's narration.** Compare the neutral relay <post>❗️Both teams, Barcelona and Manchester City, confirm they are currently in negotiations with good intentions — but it is NOT closed yet, still working things out. @moillorens #Transfers 🧘🏻‍♂️</post> — the only warmth ("good intentions") is attributed to the clubs' own confirmed stance, not offered as the writer's judgment.

- **Never let a breaking-news post run past roughly two sentences.** The three posts that exceed 280 characters are all multi-quote roundups explicitly built from a source's extended remarks (marked `long="true"` in the corpus), not single-claim breaking posts — a plain JUST IN/BREAKING item stays short.

There is no cluster in between roundups and short flashes — the writer avoids mid-length prose paragraphs that aren't either a single flash or a fully quoted multi-line roundup.

For the Quoted Source Roundup (the writer's longest mode):

OPENER (emoji cluster + "More on the [story] from @[source]:" or a bare handle credit) / QUOTE (curly-quoted sentence or two, own paragraph, optional trailing emoji) / QUOTE (repeats, 1–2 more times, optional) / CLOSER (#Transfers + topical emoji cluster, sometimes folded into the final quote's line).

Only the OPENER and at least one QUOTE block are mandatory; additional QUOTE blocks repeat as the source's statement runs on; the CLOSER is present in every example seen.

## Post Relationships

The corpus shows a running live-blog structure on one story (Rodri) rather than discrete announcement/recap pairs: each post updates the immediately preceding one, reusing the same figures (fees, club names) while upgrading the verb of certainty as the deal progresses — "negotiations underway" → "opening bid" → "guarantees given" → "terms accepted" → "agreement reached." Compare the sequence: <post>🚨💥 JUST IN: Negotiations underway between City and Barcelona for Rodri! €45m will not be enough, but Barça prepared to pay more than this. Good relationship b/w the clubs. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers ☎️🔵🔴⏳</post> followed hours later by <post>🚨🔥 BREAKING: All contractual terms now ACCEPTED by Rodri. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 💰🔵🔴✅ https://t.co/xRQz1SZYAL</post> — the club names, hashtag, and 🔵🔴 emoji carry over unchanged; only the verb and certainty level are upgraded, and a photo attachment is added once the deal is confirmed. The writer also occasionally posts a meta-commentary aside ("Calm.", "No new update, as of 11:00pm.") between hard updates to manage follower expectations mid-saga — these are not paired with a specific earlier post but function as pacing devices within the live thread.
